about: Each NESS brass instrument's standard fingerings as its players' charts give them: hard empirical data (the owner, 23 October 2026: "Standard fingerings, where standard, are hard empirical data"). For each written note (C4 middle C), its fingerings in its chart's order: the first its standard one, the rest the alternatives the chart gives. A valve fingering's valves from the first, 1 pressed and 0 not; a slide's its position (1 in, 7 out). `sounds`: semitones from the written note to the sounding one. Each read off its chart by eye (research-downloads/brass/fingering-charts/, 24 October 2026). Read by render/synthesis/src/ness.mjs chartedFingerings.

trumpet.source: Yamaha Corporation, Musical instrument guide, "Trumpet fingering chart", https://www.yamaha.com/en/musical_instrument_guide/common/images/trumpet/fingering.pdf (fetched 24 October 2026); the upper of two fingerings its standard, the lower its alternate

horn.source: Yamaha Corporation, Musical instrument guide, "Horn fingering chart", its F single horn's rows, https://www.yamaha.com/en/musical_instrument_guide/common/images/horn/fingering.pdf (fetched 24 October 2026): "When there are two fingerings for the same note, generally the fingering written to the left is used. Alternate fingering is on the right." Its bass clef in modern notation, continuous with its treble

tuba.source: N. Bewley 2008, "CC Tuba Fingering Chart, Non-Compensating 4 Valve", https://norlanbewley.com/bewleymusic/tuba-fingering-charts/4-valve-cc-tuba-nc/ (its chart www.norlanbewley.com/music/tuba-chart-2.pdf, fetched 24 October 2026); "a or b" read as a standard and its alternate. C#1 it gives none (N/A)

trombone.instrument: B-flat tenor trombone, slide (its F attachment unused by the renders)
trombone.source: Yamaha Corporation, Musical instrument guide, "Trombone fingering chart", https://www.yamaha.com/en/musical_instrument_guide/common/images/trombone/fingering.pdf (fetched 24 October 2026); a position marked "Alternate fingering" its alternate
